wage_series_reference: average_monthly_salaries.csv; pre-1992 observations use historical_manufacturing_hourly_wages.csv where available

sources.source: Statistics Sweden (SCB), average monthly salary after sector, all sectors, total gender.
sources.unit: SEK/month; annual comparator calculated as monthly × 12
sources.definition: SCB average monthly salary across all sectors, both sexes (total gender), for each year 1992–2025. Salary is not disposable income or actual annual earnings.
sources.transformation: Annual comparator is monthly average multiplied by 12; nominal values. Monthly source values retained in the separate salary file.

sources.source: Sveriges Riksbank, Historical Monetary and Financial Statistics for Sweden, Volume I, Svante Prado workbook, Tables I.A10.1 and I.A10.2.
sources.definition: Hourly earnings by manufacturing industry category and sex, plus a separately identified source-provided weighted average. Source table categories are represented in Swedish in the CSV.
sources.coverage: Sweden; manufacturing workers. Coverage varies by industry and sex. Male categories are observed from 1860 or later depending on category; female coverage starts between 1865 and 1952 by category. Male weighted average 1871–2013; female weighted average 1921–2013.
sources.transformation: Transcribed source observations without annualization or interpolation. Missing cells are omitted. This sectoral hourly series is not directly equivalent to all-sector monthly salary; overlap does not imply equivalent population or method.

sources.source: Swedish Nintendo price observations from a Milu Handels AB flyer archived by a seller and dated 1987, Larkman Computer Center catalogue in Datormagazin issue 6/91, Spelhuset/High Score Express issue 18/93, and Nordic Games advertisement in Datormagazin issue 19/94. Bergsala's 1988–1993 brochures and 1992 SNES/game guides were reviewed; they list games but do not establish prices.
sources.definition: Sparse dated source samples of nominal listed price per Nintendo game. The displayed value is the unweighted arithmetic mean of the games whose prices are documented in each source; this is not a market-wide or calendar-year mean. Platform scope and source/sample type are reported per row.
sources.coverage: Seven retailer/catalogue observations across five years: 1987 NES (12 cassette prices in one Milu Handels AB flyer dated 1987 by the archive seller; image lists each at 289 SEK), 1991 NES (51 prices in Larkman Computer Center's Datormagazin 6/91 catalogue), 1992 NES (26 titles) and SNES (10 games) from Aintronic's Datormagazin 13/92 ad, plus 1992 SNES (44 titles) from Landsbergs Spel & Data's Datormagazin 17/92 ad; 1993 SNES (17 listed prices) and 1994 SNES (9 new games). No verified values found for 1988–1990 or 1995 onward. Official-distributor brochure scans reviewed for 1988–1993 are game lists, not price lists. The 1990 Datormagazin examples at 398 SEK are in a hypothetical reader letter, not a price advertisement, and are excluded.
sources.transformation: 1987 mean is 12×289 SEK / 12 = 289 SEK; source is a surviving flyer image, and its year is attributed by the archive seller listing, so the date is less secure than a dated periodical. 1991: 51 prices total 19,125 SEK / 51 = 375.00 SEK; catalogue footer says prices include VAT and postage is extra. Aintronic 1992 sample: 26 NES prices total 9,354 / 26 = 359.77 SEK; 10 individually listed SNES games total 4,760 / 10 = 476 SEK; excludes a Super Scope 6-game pack. The Datormagazin 13/92 ad states 25% VAT is included, while postage/handling is extra. Landsbergs Spel & Data 1992 SNES sample: 44 listed titles all 499 SEK incl. VAT; some marked 'ute snart', and postage/payment fees extra. 1993: 11,133 / 17 = 654.88 SEK. 1994: 4,941 / 9 = 549.00 SEK. The sources differ by seller, platform, and sample design; no trend is inferred. Price points are nominal. Wage shares use the Riksbank male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours in 1987 and 1991; other years use SCB all-sector average monthly salary × 12. The different populations and methods are not directly comparable. No interpolation; missing price years stay gaps.

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 12 titles shown in a Milu Handels AB flyer dated 1987 by the archive seller; each cassette listed at 289 SEK. Dated single-retailer flyer, not a national or annual market mean
data.wage_basis: Riksbank historical male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours (40 × 52); not comparable to SCB all-sector salary

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 51 NES game prices in Larkman Computer Center catalogue/advertisement in Datormagazin issue 6/91; nominal listed SEK, issue dated 1991, not a market-wide annual mean
data.wage_basis: Riksbank historical male weighted-average manufacturing hourly wage × 2,080 hours (40 × 52); not comparable to SCB all-sector salary

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean of 26 original-packaged NES titles in Aintronic's Datormagazin 13/92 catalogue advertisement; prices incl. 25% VAT, postage and handling extra; 1992 issue-specific retailer sample
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean of 10 individually listed SNES games in Aintronic's Datormagazin 13/92 catalogue advertisement; excludes Super Scope 6-game pack; prices incl. 25% VAT, postage and handling extra; 1992 issue-specific retailer sample
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Arithmetic mean: 44 priced SNES titles in Landsbergs Spel & Data advertisement in Datormagazin issue 17/92; all listed at 499 SEK incl. VAT, some marked 'out soon'; mail-order postage/fees extra, not a market-wide annual mean
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Unweighted mean of 17 advertised SNES titles in a Swedish mail-order catalogue; listed selling prices, not a market-wide mean
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12

data.price_basis: Unweighted mean of 9 SNES games explicitly listed as new in a Swedish mail-order advertisement; seller describes its prices as low mail-order prices, not a market-wide mean
data.wage_basis: SCB average monthly salary, all sectors, total gender × 12
